title: TileLink: Generating Efficient Compute-Communication Overlapping Kernels using Tile-Centric Primitives
problem: Distributed LLM training and inference require overlapping compute with inter-GPU communication (all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter) to hide network latency. Operator decomposition is easy but leaves performance on the table; fusing communication into compute kernels is effective but requires expert CUDA/NVSHMEM code that is error-prone and non-portable.
motivation: Existing overlapping libraries like FLUX require ~2000 lines of hand-written CUDA. Decomposed operator approaches that simply pipeline communication stages achieve lower utilization because they cannot finely interleave compute and communication tiles. A compiler abstraction that decouples the two concerns and synthesizes fused kernels would lower the expertise barrier while matching expert-tuned performance.
method: TileLink has a frontend and a backend. The frontend exposes tile-centric primitives: producer_tile_notify/consumer_tile_wait synchronize tile-level data readiness; peer_tile_notify/peer_tile_wait coordinate cross-rank tile dependencies; tile_push_data/tile_pull_data transfer tiles between devices; rank_copy_data/rank_notify/rank_wait handle rank-level collective coordination. The backend performs tile-centric mapping in three stages: (1) shape mapping assigns tile dimensions to compute and communication workloads; (2) rank mapping determines which GPU rank computes/receives each tile via affine transforms (static) or runtime lookup tables (dynamic); (3) channel mapping assigns each tile to an NVLink/InfiniBand channel. The backend compiles these mappings to PTX via Triton extended with NVSHMEM primitives, producing fused kernels that interleave compute threads and communication threads within a single CUDA kernel.
key_novelty: Tile-centric primitive abstraction that decouples compute and communication design spaces at the tile granularity, compiled to overlapping kernels via shape/rank/channel mapping; achieves expert-level overlap with ~10x less code than handwritten CUDA.
contributions: Tile-centric frontend primitives (9 ops) that decouple compute-communication design space
Three-stage backend: shape mapping, rank mapping (affine or lookup-table), channel mapping
Compilation to PTX via Triton+NVSHMEM for generating fused overlapping kernels
Support for static (affine) and dynamic (lookup-table) rank mapping for irregular collectives
Demonstration on GEMM+all-reduce, GEMM+all-gather, MoE expert dispatch, and attention+communication

metrics.vs_flux: Performance comparable to FLUX (expert-written library) with ~200 Python lines vs ~2000 CUDA lines
metrics.code_reduction: ~10x less code than equivalent FLUX implementation

limitations: Static shape mapping requires recompilation for different tensor shapes
Dynamic lookup-table mapping adds runtime overhead for irregular collectives
NVSHMEM dependency limits portability to non-NVIDIA interconnects
Tile granularity must be tuned per model architecture and hardware topology
